### current community. ### your communities. ### more stack exchange communities. Communities for your favorite technologies. Stack Overflow for Teams is now called **Stack Internal**. ##### Collectives™ on Stack Overflow. # Understanding gitlab ci artifacts, using with nightwatchjs. I'm not really following the artifacts part of gitlab ci too well, and every attempt to do what i want doesn't work. I have a build and test stage, the build stage uses the Dockerfile in my project to build and image and push to registry, the test stage then uses the image to run nightwatch tests. The dockerfile basically installs chrome and other things needed for the nightwatch test. I need to be able to get hold of screenshots nightwatch takes during the tests and i thought artifacts would do that but i never end up with screenshots in the downloaded zip, only empty folders. - docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t myusername/myimage:latest . - docker image push myusername/myimage:latest. - cd /var/tests/ && nightwatch --env int --test tests/my-test.js`. So the code is all taken into /var/tests from when the dockerfile builds the image. I have a WORKDIR set in the image to /var/tests so i assumed that artifacts would be mapped to /var/tests/screenshots but it clearly isn't - or there are some file writing issues in the container it runs? ## 1 Answer 1. By default, GitLab runs commands in the `/builds/<project-path>` directory. See, GitLab Docs: Docker: Where scripts are executed. Verify this by putting `- pwd` at the top of the `scripts:` section of `.gitlab-ci.yml`, and watching the output of the job. Typically, all CI/CD commands should be run from the container's `WORKDIR`, the path within the container where you copied your code. So, simply `cd /path/to/workdir` as the first command in your script. Artifact paths should be relative to your `WORKDIR`. ## Your Answer. Thanks for contributing an answer to Stack Overflow! Title: Docker for Data Engineers:Patterns,Examples & Tips | Python in Plain English
## Python in Plain English. New Python content every day. Follow to join our 3.5M+ monthly readers. # Docker for Data Engineers: Reproducible Pipelines, Portable Stacks, Production-Ready. Press enter or click to view image in full size. Docker for Data Engineer Image. ## Why Docker matters in data engineering ? Data is messy, environments are messier. Python versions drift, native libs differ, drivers mismatch, JVMs vary. Docker packages ***exact versions*** of everything your job needs (runtime + dependencies + drivers) into an ***image***. You run that image as a ***container*** anywhere: your laptop, a build agent, or a production cluster. Outcome: fewer environment bugs, faster onboarding, and consistent results. * ***Reproducibility:***Bake your runtime (Python/Java/OS libs) into images so “works on my machine” disappears. * ***Portable stacks:*** Use ***Docker Compose*** to spin up Kafka, Postgres, MinIO/S3, Airflow/Prefect, Spark, and a notebook with one command. * ***Quality gates:*** Run integration tests against ephemeral containers in CI before merging. * ***Ops-ready:***Ship small, secure images; externalize config; manage data with volumes; stream logs. * ***Scale path:*** Same image runs locally, in CI, and in prod (Kubernetes, ECS, ACI, etc.). ### Core concepts:. Think: *Python 3.11 + libs + your code*. * ***Container******:*** A running instance of an image (ephemeral by default). * ***Dockerfile******:*** How to build the image (install libs, copy code). * ***Compose******:*** One YAML that defines a ***stack*** (services + networks + volumes). * ***Volumes******:*** Persistent data (databases, object storage emulators). * ***Networks******:*** Private DNS and connectivity between services. * ***.******env******:*** Centralize secrets & env vars (never commit real secrets). ### A practical local data stack (Compose):. Spin up a realistic playground for ELT + streaming + files — great for dev and integration tests. # docker-compose.ymlversion: "3.9"services:  postgres:    image: postgres:15    environment:      POSTGRES_USER: app      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: app      POSTGRES_DB: warehouse    ports: ["5432:5432"]    volumes: [pg:/var/lib/postgresql/data]  minio:    image…. ## Published in Python in Plain English. ·Last published 22 hours ago. results.content:
Title: Running Unit Tests With Docker
# Running Unit Tests With Docker. How to use the same container to run… | by Leonardo Lima | The Startup | Medium. ## The Startup. # Running Unit Tests With Docker. ## How to use the same container to run and test your application. And Docker is like a universal language, there is multiple tools that can work with it, like Kubernetes, Google Cloud Run, AWS ECS, etc. When we use a CI tool, we usually build and run tests outside a Container, but there is an easy way to do everything inside. This is specially useful when you are using tools like GitHub Actions or Jenkins, then you need to build your application only once and use your Docker image to test and deploy anywhere else. I will be writing a simple Hello World code, a test, and a Dockerfile for it. I’m using Golang, but you can use the same for any language, you just need to know the commands to run and test it. I made a GitHub repository with some code examples for multiple languages, feel free to check it out:. ## leozz37/docker-unit-tests ### You can't perform that action at this time. Note that we use `CMD` to run our application, so when we use the `docker run`command it will run normally. Now to run our application, we need to build and run it, like this:. -t medium-example$ docker run medium-example. Now to run our tests, we just pass `sh -c "TEST_COMMAND"` after the docker run command. $ docker run medium-example sh -c "go test". The `sh -c` let you run any command inside your container. If you a have a `CMD` or `entrypoint` setup, it will overwrite it. If you have a multi-stage build, you need to make sure your code files are presente in the last stage and that you command can "see them". If you have a different user to run your binary/code, make sure it has permission to run your tests. One last tip, you can make a script to run multiple kind of tests and do the same strategy to execute it. ## Published in The Startup.
